questions.stem: Why is random sampling important in ecological investigations?

options.text: It ensures every organism is counted individually
It avoids bias so that results are representative of the whole area
It makes the investigation quicker to carry out
It guarantees that all species will be found

questions.explanation: Random sampling avoids bias in data collection. If samples are not random, the investigator might unconsciously choose areas that are not representative of the whole habitat, leading to unreliable conclusions about the population.
